# Resistance Hydrodynamics Laboratory (RHL), Inha University

> Ship hydrodynamics research group at Inha University, Incheon, Korea, led by
> Prof. Soonseok Song. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is our primary tool;
> towing-tank and flow-channel experiments validate it. Marine renewable energy
> is a second major strand.

Note: http://rhl.inha.ac.kr forwards here via a meta refresh. This site
(https://soonseok-song.github.io) is the canonical, crawlable address.

## Research areas
- Roughness effect & ship hydrodynamics: biofouling, antifouling coatings, roughness functions, similarity-law scaling, modified wall-function CFD at full scale
- 6-DOF ship manoeuvring: free-running CFD in waves, steering and engine failure, trim effects, fin-stabiliser control
- Energy saving devices: air lubrication systems, wind-assisted propulsion, rotor sails, software-in-the-loop towing-tank tests
- Arctic ships: coupled CFD-DEM ice-floe simulation, ice tank model tests
- Floating offshore wind turbines: CFD-MoorDyn coupling, mooring-line failure, actuator line method for rotor wakes, AI-CFD coupling
- Tidal turbines: performance, scale effects, wave-induced loading
- Applied & environmental hydrodynamics: dissolved-oxygen transport in aquaculture, scour around marine structures

Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering, Inha University. PhD, University of
Strathclyde (2020). s.song@inha.ac.kr
